issues.classification: sealed skipped-case streams bypass canonical/canary verification
issues.finding: The common evidence loader converts invalid skipped-case public streams to empty rows with invalid=false. The upload verifier consumes that sanitized representation instead of rejecting the actual noncanonical sealed file whose bytes will be uploaded. Manifest equality authenticates the unsafe bytes, not their safe schema.

static_counterexample.baseline: Any otherwise valid T0/T1-success sealed directory from the source fixture; T2/T3 are genuine skipped cases with empty streams.
static_counterexample.integrity_update: Update only the matching manifest bytes and SHA-256 to the replacement file; all other files/fields remain unchanged.
static_counterexample.path: readOwned and manifest digest comparison accept its bounded regular-file bytes; parseRows rejects the canary; loadCaseEvidence skipped branch returns rows=[], text="", invalid=false; the canonical assertion and skipped-case validator now see an empty safe stream, while explicit upload still targets the unchanged raw file.
static_counterexample.statically_derived_result: The verifier has no remaining condition that rejects this canary-bearing skipped stream. This is a source-path proof, not an executed verifier test.

issues.scope_distinction: Rebuilding invalid scratch evidence to empty public files during seal is allowed. Treating invalid already-sealed bytes as empty during verify-upload is not. The verifier does not overwrite the actual file, so those unsafe bytes survive for upload.
minimum_fix: Within the existing new CLI, separate scratch reconstruction from sealed-file validation, or provide a strict sealed-loader mode that rejects any invalid stream before the skipped-case empty-stream branch.
Require actual sealed guard/trace bytes to be canonical and empty for a skipped case; do not erase invalid flags.

In the existing new test file, cover each skipped guard/trace path with unsafe/canary/noncanonical bytes and a refreshed valid manifest; immediate verification must reject without rewriting the sealed files.

issues.classification: failed owned-PID observation is treated as known absence
issues.finding: Both live-PID samples collapse every process.kill(pid,0) exception to false. A failed observation becomes empty possible-live sets and may become cleanupUnknown=false, a complete clean T1/T2 observation, progression and root deletion. Unsupported/permission errors do not establish a dead PID.

static_counterexample.admitted_case: T1 clean api-return/refused status=1 with empty prefix, or T2 same refusal with json-enter-only prefix; all other tuple/identity/EOF/health/counter inputs canonical.
static_counterexample.uncertain_observation: A zero-signal query for an observed owned PID throws EPERM or another non-absence observation error in both samples.
static_counterexample.current_path: sample catch returns false twice -> liveAtReturn=[] and liveAfter=[] -> cleanupUnknown expression has no sampling-unknown term -> rootRetained=false -> evaluateCase can declare complete -> selection admits T2/T3 -> rmSync deletes the root.
static_counterexample.statically_derived_result: An unknown cleanup observation can authorize progression and deletion. No EPERM or native process behavior was induced in this review.

issues.inherited_behavior_limit: The frozen earlier CLI contains a similar coarse catch. That historical implementation is not a waiver of the locked new-spec requirement that cleanup remain independently trustworthy; it is not modified by this review.
minimum_fix: In the existing new CLI, keep an independent sample-unknown flag or a tri-state sample. Treat only a positively recognized absent-process result as known absence; non-absence or unsupported query errors remain unknown.
Propagate any sampling uncertainty to cleanupUnknown/rootRetained and incomplete observation, without changing deadlines, signaling historical evidence PIDs, scanning names or adding native queries.
Add a diagnostic-local mocked sampling-error control at both T1/T2 boundaries: no progression, retained root, incomplete observation.

issues.classification: parser-invalid stream masks independent missing-EOF retention
issues.finding: Recorder precedence correctly classifies parser violations as invalid even when EOF is missing. The case evaluator only retains a root for stream.state=unknown, however, not for explicit missing EOF in an invalid stream. Invalidity blocks progression but can leave cleanupUnknown=false/rootRetained=false and delete an EOF-unknown root.

static_counterexample.base: A T1 canonical returned-refusal/owned four-exit-close tuple with empty marker prefix, trusted root/health/counter inputs.
static_counterexample.path: This exact safe stream-end shape passes evidenceEvent; stageFacts returns valid=false but preserves the stream. evaluateCase sets diagnostic_observation_complete=false, yet its retention condition sees neither missing stream nor state=unknown. Supplied cleanupUnknown=false/rootRetained=false remain unchanged. runCase then deletes the root.
static_counterexample.statically_derived_result: Missing EOF is overridden for cleanup retention by parser-invalid state. Selection does stop; this finding is about independent uncertainty and root preservation, not an extra native launch.

minimum_fix: In the existing new CLI, derive EOF uncertainty independently of parser-state precedence and force cleanupUnknown/rootRetained when either actual EOF is unobserved, including invalid/overflow stream states.
Keep invalid state and its first parser reason; do not relabel it as clean or replace it with fabricated EOF.
Add a combined invalid-plus-missing-EOF control proving incomplete observation and retained root at the actual case/cleanup boundary.
